arguments.name: From conscious value to moral authority
premises: There are subjects to whom conditions can be good or bad.
Assume reasons to protect subjects are objective, not merely reports of desire.
Propose one necessarily good personal foundation whose relation to agents grounds binding demands.
bridge_principles: Valence or flourishing has normative significance.
Relevant others count even when helping them conflicts with my aims.
The foundation is the relevant good, and its relation supplies legitimate authority.
Commands are identifiable and consistent with that nature.
arguments.conclusion: The full account could unify welfare, reasons, obligations and accountability if every bridge is warranted; consciousness alone proves none of the later bridges.
arguments.strongest_objection: Calling a being good or creative may presuppose the normativity being explained; unity and sanctions can yield only self-interest.
arguments.strongest_reply: Grounding need not be a definition or a temporal production: a defensible identity/constitution account can terminate explanation in a necessary good and a legitimate relation. This reply still owes warrant for that identity and relation.
unresolved_issues: No derivation of impartiality from mere awareness.
No independent authority proof in inspected Craig transcript.
No assumption that divine commands all have identical modal status.
arguments.authorship: Project-authored reconstruction; source attributions confined to linked claims.

arguments.name: Secular moral objectivity and its explanatory costs
arguments.position: Positive naturalistic account with other secular families retained
premises: Human and animal conditions can affect their interests independently of current approval.
A proposed moral standard considers all affected interests impartially.
Correctness can diverge from present preference and social convention.
bridge_principles: Identify the proposed natural property with normative goodness or rightness, with semantic and explanatory warrant.
Justify impartiality and the treatment of conflicting interests.
arguments.conclusion: A physicalist ontology has a substantive route to moral realism; this route remains contested and does not settle every categorical-reason demand.
arguments.strongest_objection: A fully informed egoist may still reject impartiality; reliable preference explanation might explain moral belief while omitting moral authority.
arguments.strongest_reply: Separate truth and applicability from the agent’s motivation; evaluate whether the proposed identity explains correction, practical criticism and disagreement. Other secular accounts can instead take categorical reasons or rational agency as basic, with their own costs.
unresolved_issues: Naturalism is not a proof from evolution.
Constructivism and non-natural realism reconstructed in matrix but no decisive original defender inspected.
Aggregative criterion may face rights, comparability and determinate-idealization objections.

arguments.name: Suffering as evidence against specified perfect governance
arguments.position: Evidential challenge, distinct from bare logical incompatibility
premises: Assume an agent knows the relevant harms and feasible alternatives, can prevent them and is perfectly good.
Some suffering appears to lack a permission-justifying dependence on goods or avoidance of comparable evil.
bridge_principles: Our inability to find such dependence is defeasible evidence of its absence in the relevant domain.
A perfectly good agent does not permit harms without adequate justification; equal-value and irreplaceability qualifications must be specified.
arguments.conclusion: Suffering challenges that attribute package if the evidential and normative premises hold; it is not a deduction from the mere occurrence of any evil.
arguments.strongest_objection: Our sample of goods, causal relations and feasible worlds may be too limited to assess what an omniscient being could justifiably permit.
arguments.strongest_reply: Finite limits do not automatically erase all evidence; compare what each hypothesis actually leads us to expect and what independently supports claimed limitations. Theistic countergrounds can rationally matter.
unresolved_issues: No measured prevalence or likelihood supplied.
A hypothetical animal does not establish an actual event.
Free-will and soul-making originals beyond the inspected discussions remain gaps.

arguments.name: Restoration of persons and justification of harm
arguments.position: Strong enduring-restoration reply and victim-centered challenge
premises: Assume the same victims continue and receive goods capable of restoring meaningful lives.
Assume their harms can be integrated without denying their reality or replacing victims with successors.
bridge_principles: A good total life or meaningful integration can answer some questions about final loss.
Antecedent permission requires a separate justification, including necessity, proportionality, rights and alternatives where applicable.
arguments.conclusion: Restoration can improve an account of what becomes of victims, while an account of why harms were permitted remains independently contestable.
arguments.strongest_objection: A later good may quiet grief without making the original injustice permissible; one person’s reconciliation cannot speak for another victim.
arguments.strongest_reply: The strongest version addresses each victim and distinguishes redemption from approval of wrongdoing; an internal consistency defense may use its own independently specified goods without claiming their actual existence is thereby proved.
unresolved_issues: The possibility and worth of divine intimacy remain contested.
Identity and temporal manifestation must be specified.
Adams’s later clarifications and reply to Sutherland not inspected.

arguments.name: Nonresistant nonbelief and relationship
arguments.position: Hiddenness challenge with a bounded, currently reconstructed reply
premises: Assume perfect love includes being open to conscious reciprocal relationship with each capable person.
Assume belief in the other’s existence is required for that specified relationship.
Assume some capable persons lack belief for causes unrelated to resisting that relationship.
bridge_principles: Perfect love entails that availability at each relevant time, rather than only eventual welfare or eventual access.
arguments.conclusion: If the premises hold, the specified perfectly loving personal God is excluded; other ultimate foundations remain open.
arguments.strongest_objection: Howard-Snyder distinguishes a desire for relationship now from an overriding reason to enable it now. Even a well-disposed inculpable seeker might benefit from owning or refining the disposition to love. He offers defeasible prima facie reasons and epistemic caution, not proof of actual divine reasons.
arguments.strongest_reply: Project comparison: a possible counterfactual disposition is not automatically resistance causing present nonbelief. Ask whether improving love can occur in an available relationship, and whether delaying access is no worse than other means once the lost relationship is counted. A defender may contest that comparison or our knowledge of it. Note18 and reply4 identify limits to this particular defense; no blanket victory is inferred.
unresolved_issues: The1996reply addresses earlier Schellenberg; the2025argument emphasizes nonresistance causally relevant to nonbelief. Exact earlier book/reply exchange not inspected.
A reason to delay developing a relationship does not automatically explain withholding the conditions of being open to one; this is the contested bridge.
No observed distribution of dispositions or actual divine permission reasons.
Availability, fittingness and the no-worse-alternative criterion remain disputed.

arguments.name: Goodness, authority and dependence across the package
premises: Value judgments support the moral-grounding proposal and also underwrite evil objections.
Knowledge of goodness and permission-justifying reasons can have different scope.
Claims of actual survival or intended moral education need evidence apart from their usefulness in a reply.
bridge_principles: Avoid counting the same moral premise as independent evidence each time it recurs.
Apply explanatory stopping-point and epistemic-access standards symmetrically to divine and secular accounts.
arguments.conclusion: This packet maps burdens for H-G and H-A, with conditional effects on H-I/P/S; it identifies neither a numerical posterior nor a winning full metaphysics.
arguments.strongest_objection: Restricting knowledge of unknown goods need not undermine simple moral knowledge; criticism can demand unreasonable omniscience of the defender.
arguments.strongest_reply: Use local rather than blanket skepticism and name what remains knowable; test whether the positive and negative inferences genuinely rely on the same inaccessible domain.
unresolved_issues: Removing retrospective NDE claims leaves conceptual distinctions but no new survival evidence.
Rejecting moral realism changes the moral argument and some evil formulations; internal inconsistency arguments can still use an opponent’s commitments.
